- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.surround

### Question

In nvim.surround, there is the option to move the surrounding to a seperate line. E.g. when using `ySiw}` instead of `ysiw}` (capital S) on a word I would transform
```
some_word
```
to
```
{
    some_word
}
```
Is there a similar option in mini.surround? I didn't find anything in the docs

comment_data.body:
Yes, this is possible in 'mini.surround' to a certain extent via [`config.respect_selection_type`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/05975f387906211745d0aaf996eb7ad3c91b193d/doc/mini-surround.txt#L517-L520). See more description [here](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/05975f387906211745d0aaf996eb7ad3c91b193d/doc/mini-surround.txt#L630).

This particular case would work via `sa_}`, as it requires linewise movement/selection (while `iw` is charwise).

reply_data.body: Using `saiw{` or `saiw}` works as described [here](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/05975f387906211745d0aaf996eb7ad3c91b193d/doc/mini-surround.txt#L73), but if you want to include newlines in the surrounding, as mentioned [here](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/05975f387906211745d0aaf996eb7ad3c91b193d/doc/mini-surround.txt#L598-L617), you should use `{\n` and `\n}` instead.
reply_data.bodyHTML: Using saiw{ or saiw} works as described here, but if you want to include newlines in the surrounding, as mentioned here, you should use {\n and \n} instead.

reply_data.bodyHTML:
... how would I do that?

Unfortunately, there is no easy way to do this, as usually mixing charwise and linewise operations (as this makes charwise selection appear on separate lines with new indent) is up to no good.

The best feasible solution is to follow @krovuxdev's suggestion and dedicate a special identifier for such cases. However, using only {\n and \n} is not enough as it will not keep indent, which is the real problem here. So this would require something like this:

require('mini.surround').setup({
  custom_surroundings = {
    ['{'] = {
      output = function()
        local indent = vim.api.nvim_get_current_line():match('^%s*')
        local sw = vim.bo.shiftwidth
        local tab_text = vim.bo.expandtab and string.rep(' ', sw == 0 and vim.bo.tabstop or sw) or '\t'
        return { left = '{\n' .. indent .. tab_text, right = '\n' .. indent .. '}' }
      end,
    },
  },
})

Note that } will still insert { and } without whitespaces, as is built-in.

reply_data.bodyHTML:
Would it maybe make sense to add smilar behavior from nivm.surround to mini.surround?

Not really. Mostly because it doesn't play nicely with deleting and replacing surrounds. To achieve that, there would have to be something like sA, sD, sR mappings, which I am not sure I like to have.

Because if I map it like that I can't use the builtin berhavior of { anymore (unless I bind it to another key of course).

Do you frequently need all three variants (without spaces, with single space, on separate line), though? Even if the answer is yes, there are still a lot of spare identifiers. If you want to have this kind of behavior for multiple brackets, that is also possible with something like this:

local brackets = {
  ['('] = { '(', ')' },
  ['['] = { '[', ']' },
  ['{'] = { '{', '}' },
  ['<'] = { '<', '>' },
}
require('mini.surround').setup({
  custom_surroundings = {
    ['n'] = {
      output = function()
        local id = vim.fn.getcharstr()
        local left, right = unpack(brackets[id])
        local indent = vim.api.nvim_get_current_line():match('^%s*')
        local sw = vim.bo.shiftwidth
        local tab_text = vim.bo.expandtab and string.rep(' ', sw == 0 and vim.bo.tabstop or sw) or '\t'
        return { left = left .. '\n' .. indent .. tab_text, right = '\n' .. indent .. right }
      end,
    },
  },
})

Now doing sa-iw-n( will surround with new lines while keeping indents. Maybe making this special surrounding built-in would make sense, but my initial reaction is that this is too much to be built-in. Maybe as a wiki entry in the future.
